headline: Cohesin bridging and MD simulations probe enhancer-promoter and nucleic acid recognition
label: Chromatin Polymer Structure Modeling
summary: Simulation-based models now span chromatin looping, spliceosomal branch-site recognition, engineered RNA design, and glycosylase lesion recognition.
synthesis: The dominant thread is physics-based modeling of how conformational coupling and mechanical constraints govern nucleic acid function. A preprint proposes cohesin bridging during loop extrusion as a physical route for enhancer-promoter communication, supported by a quantitative model of transcriptional output. Three published studies apply molecular dynamics to nucleic acid machinery: a loaded-spring latching mechanism in which TAT-SF1 release of the U2 snRNA branch-stem loop drives toehold-mediated strand invasion; mechanics-aware design of exoribonuclease-resistant RNAs that stall XRN1; and enhanced-sampling free energy landscapes for MutY lesion recognition via a linker-coordinated pathway. What is new is the explicit treatment of stored mechanical energy and topological constraints as functional elements, rather than purely structural description.
